draft.name: Iterative Refinement Cycle
draft.definition: A cyclical process involving generation, critical review, and provision of feedback to improve an output until desired quality is achieved.
draft.mechanism: The process involves generating an initial output, subjecting it to critical evaluation against requirements, and then providing specific feedback or a refined prompt to guide the next iteration.
draft.boundary: The cycle begins with an initial generation and continues through successive rounds of review and refinement until the desired outcome is reached.
draft.consequence: The successful application of this cycle leads to improved output quality, potentially surpassing the individual capabilities of components when collaboration is involved.

Within months, the water has crossed the local chasm from the early adopters to the rest of the village.

draft.name: Network Effect Adoption
draft.definition: The process where the value of a product or service increases proportionally to the number of users who use it.
draft.mechanism: The presence of early adopters creates a critical mass (e.g., clean water in a village) which, once established, causes subsequent users to adopt due to social pressure or increased utility, leading to the isolation of those who do not adopt.
draft.boundary: The transition from early adopters to the broader market/village.
draft.consequence: Social isolation or feeling 'stupid' among those who lag in adoption.

draft.name: Backpropagation
draft.definition: A process used to adjust weights and biases in neural networks based on classification errors or desired outputs.
draft.mechanism: Errors are computed (e.g., classification error) and then propagated backward through the network to update the parameters (weights and biases) of the layers, seeking to minimize error (in discriminators) or maximize error (in generators).
draft.boundary: The process begins with an output/error signal and flows backward through the network layers to adjust parameters. In sparse models (like MoEs), gradient flow is restricted only to activated experts.
draft.consequence: Successful application leads to the network learning to encode relationships (e.g., word similarities in embeddings) or achieving convergence toward a desired state (e.g., minimizing classification error).

draft.name: Convergence to Normal Distribution
draft.definition: A tendency for data distributions or model representations to approximate a normal (Gaussian) distribution.
draft.mechanism: This is an empirical/descriptive pattern, not a causal mechanism
draft.boundary: The degree of overlap between classes or the statistical significance threshold (e.g., p > 0.05 for Gaussian assumption).
draft.consequence: Achieving a better-behaved result centered around zero, or failing to reject the null hypothesis that the data is Gaussian.
